blocks.content: Lakshadweep's remoteness makes connectivity infrastructure a uniquely central policy theme — this chapter covers the major recent projects and schemes, several directly tied to the 2024 tourism-boom context described in Chapter 5.

cells: Lakshadweep's only operational airport, on Agatti Island, connecting the territory to Kochi and other mainland destinations; the small runway size has historically restricted aircraft size and flight frequency

Passenger and cargo ships operated by the Lakshadweep Administration connect Kavaratti and other islands to Kochi; given limited air connectivity, ships remain a vital lifeline for both passenger travel and goods transport

A submarine cable connectivity project, commissioned in the early 2020s, bringing high-speed broadband to Kavaratti and other islands for the first time, significantly upgrading the territory's digital connectivity from earlier satellite-based systems

Various proposals for expanded air connectivity (including potential new/expanded airstrips on additional islands) have been discussed as part of the broader post-2024 tourism-development push, though implementation has been gradual given the environmental and land-constraint sensitivities involved

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: The Kochi-Lakshadweep Submarine Optical Fibre Cable (KLI SOFC) is a frequently tested recent-infrastructure fact, directly parallel to similar submarine-cable projects extended to other Indian island territories (compare the CANI cable to Andaman & Nicobar Islands, covered in the companion volume for that UT).

items: Central flagship schemes — including Ayushman Bharat, PM Awas Yojana, and Jal Jeevan Mission — have been extended to Lakshadweep, with implementation adapted to the territory's unique small-island logistical constraints.

The Lakshadweep Development Corporation Limited (LDCL), a UT-administration public-sector undertaking, plays a central role in infrastructure and tourism-facility development across the islands, working alongside the Society for Promotion of Recreational Tourism and Sports (SPORTS), the administration's dedicated tourism-promotion body.

Desalination and renewable-energy (particularly solar) infrastructure projects have been prioritised in recent years, addressing both the freshwater-scarcity challenge described in Chapter 8 and the islands' broader energy self-sufficiency needs given their remoteness from mainland power grids.
Agatti Aerodrome = Lakshadweep's only airport; ships remain a vital lifeline given limited air connectivity.
Kochi-Lakshadweep Submarine Optical Fibre Cable (KLI SOFC) brought high-speed broadband to the islands in the early 2020s.
LDCL (Lakshadweep Development Corporation) and SPORTS (tourism promotion body) are key UT-administration institutions.
Desalination and solar-energy projects address freshwater scarcity and energy self-sufficiency needs.
